summary: Build 107 Apple Review fix — testing reveals 1 CRITICAL frontend regression that DOES NOT FIX the Apple Guideline 2.1 issue. Backend (7/7 tests PASS) and most frontend checks PASS: no external links, demo button prefills correctly, dashboard reachable with 3 demo chantiers (M. Lefèvre / Mme Dubois / Dr. Martin). BUT the i18n error translation does not work in EN/NL because the frontend prefers the raw backend detail string over the i18n key. With language=EN, submitting a wrong password shows Alert title='Error' (correctly translated) but body='Email ou mot de passe incorrect' (FRENCH, identical to the message Apple flagged in Build 106). This is the very bug Build 107 is meant to fix — it is NOT fixed.

minor.issue: Backend returns French-only error message 'Email ou mot de passe incorrect' (auth.py:438,442). Frontend i18n logic depends on this, so a cleaner fix would be to either (a) return a structured detail `{code: 'invalid_credentials'}` so the frontend can localise, or (b) honour Accept-Language header. Currently the backend forces French regardless of client language.

ui_bugs.issue: BLOCKER for Apple Review (Guideline 2.1). At /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:261-268 the branch order is wrong: `if (typeof detail === 'string') msg = detail; else if (status === 401) msg = t('auth.loginErrors.invalidCredentials');` — because the backend ALWAYS sends `detail` as a French string on 401, the i18n key is NEVER used. Reviewer with EN selected will see French error body. Fix: swap branches — check `status === 401` FIRST and use the i18n key; only fall back to `detail` string when status is not 401. Verified live: window.alert captured = 'Error\n\nEmail ou mot de passe incorrect' after EN switch + wrong password.

action_items: [Optional — defence in depth] Change backend at /app/backend/routes/auth.py:438,442 to raise HTTPException(401, detail={'code': 'invalid_credentials'}) so the frontend always sees a non-string detail and can route exclusively via i18n. (If applied, also update any other consumers parsing this detail.)
[Doc fix — non-blocking] Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: the tech account password is `tech123`, NOT `admin123` as the file currently states (the conftest already uses the correct value).
[Cleanup — non-blocking] Backend logs show repeated 'passlib bcrypt __about__ AttributeError' warnings (trapped, non-fatal). Consider pinning bcrypt<4 or upgrading passlib to silence the warning.
critical_code_review_comments: The catch block in onSubmit uses `e?.response?.data?.detail` but the special-case `detail?.code === 'email_not_verified'` (line 253) will silently fail when detail is a string — `'string'?.code` is undefined which is fine, but the structure assumption is fragile. Consider always returning detail as an object from the backend for consistency.
Trim() is correctly applied on both email and password (lines 193-194) before signIn() — addresses the iPad keyboard parasitic-whitespace concern from the rejection note.
Demo button is correctly NOT conditioned on Platform.OS === 'ios' (lines 784-799), so it is visible on the web preview used for testing, as documented in the agent-to-agent context note.
No remaining import of `expo-web-browser` and no `openRegistrationWebsite` function in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx — Guideline 4 surface fix is correct.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of Apple Guideline 2.1 5th rejection persistence: In /app/frontend/app/index.tsx onSubmit catch block (lines 261-268), the branch `if (typeof detail === 'string') msg = detail;` is evaluated BEFORE the 401 i18n branch. Since /app/backend/routes/auth.py:438,442 raises `HTTPException(401, 'Email ou mot de passe incorrect')` — a plain French string — the first branch always wins for invalid-credentials cases, so `t('auth.loginErrors.invalidCredentials')` is dead code. Reproduction: viewport 390x844 → click [data-testid="auth-lang-en"] → fill applereview@mesurechassis.com + bad password → submit → window.alert captured = 'Error\n\nEmail ou mot de passe incorrect'. Mitigation: reorder the if-chain so 401 is checked first (see action_items). Build 107 i18n keys are correct in fr/en/nl.json — only the priority logic is wrong.
